report:
## Conclusion

Yes, the additional offer of HIV self-testing (HIVST) does cause more people to take an HIV test. Multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews consistently demonstrate that offering HIVST increases HIV testing uptake, frequency, and the number of new diagnoses compared to standard HIV testing services alone.

### Key Evidence

- A **systematic review and meta-analysis** of RCTs found **moderate-quality evidence** that HIVST increases the uptake of HIV testing and low-quality evidence that it increases testing frequency, compared to standard testing services. HIVST was also found to be safe, with no negative effects on condom use or substantial increases in social harm ([JIAS, 2017](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.7448/IAS.20.1.21594)).

- An updated **WHO-informing systematic review** of RCTs (published 2006–2019) concluded that HIVST increased testing uptake, frequency, and overall positivity rates among key populations (MSM and trans people) compared to standard testing ([BMC Medicine, 2020](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12916-020-01835-z)).

- A **cluster-randomized trial** in Malawi found that facility-based HIV self-testing resulted in **more than three times** the absolute number of newly diagnosed HIV-positive individuals compared to standard testing approaches ([The Lancet Global Health, 2020](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/langlo/article/PIIS2214-109X(19)30534-0/fulltext)).

- The **WHO** endorses HIVST distribution through diverse community and facility channels, noting that multiple delivery models are effective in increasing testing uptake and reaching undiagnosed individuals ([WHO Self-Testing Toolkit](https://www.who.int/tools/self-testing-implementation-toolkit-for-hiv-hcv-and-syphilis/distribution--models-for-self-testing)).

### Summary

The evidence is robust across populations and settings: adding HIV self-testing to existing testing options reliably increases the number of people who get tested, including among hard-to-reach groups. This supports WHO recommendations to integrate HIVST into national HIV testing strategies.
